```{r setup, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = TRUE,

  fig.width = 8,

)

library(dplyr)
library(stringr)
library(data.table)
library(ggplot2)
library(cowplot)
library(airr)
library(Seurat)
library(SeuratObject)
library(scoper)
library(dowser)
library(alakazam)

hunter_dir <- "/Volumes/HoehnK/Hunter"

chinmay_dir <- "/Volumes/HoehnK/Chinmay"

sirap_dir <- file.path(hunter_dir, "spatial_bcr_tcr_package", "SIRAP")
thymus_dir <- file.path(hunter_dir, "Thymus_Spatial")
walkthrough_dir <- file.path(thymus_dir, "sirap_lab_vignette", "mg_thymus_slice2")
dir.create(walkthrough_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

devtools::load_all(sirap_dir, quiet = TRUE)

sample_id <- "KH02"
dataset <- "mg_thymus_slice2"
nproc <- 2
image_scale <- "lowres"
swap_coords <- TRUE # For standard Visium objects, the coordinates need to be swapped to get the correct shape
```

Starting with RAD-processed output for Visium thymus (igblast_bcr.tsv)
slice 2.  We'll take a full tour of SIRAP and the major functionality.

# Start with the RAD/IgBLAST output

The starting BCR table is the direct IgBLAST output made after RAD
demultiplexing.

The full data is like 30G, so we're only loading 10k sequences to see how the processing
works. Once we have the data, we run `extractSpatialBarcode`, which is just a convenience
function that extracts a barcode from a column (sequence_id_col) using a regex expression
(regex) and then makes a new column (barcode_col).

```{r read-rad-output}
raw_bcr_path <- file.path(
  chinmay_dir,
  "101724_KH02_compiled_out",
  "igblast_data",
  "igblast_bcr_10k.tsv"
)

# This is a 24 GB read-level table, so we just get 10k sequences
raw_bcrs <- data.table::fread(
  raw_bcr_path,
  data.table = FALSE,
  nThread = nproc,
  showProgress = FALSE
)

raw_bcrs <- extractSpatialBarcode(
  raw_bcrs,
  sequence_id_col = "sequence_id",
  barcode_col = "barcode",
  regex = "\\|barcode:([ACGT]{16})(?:\\||$)"
)

raw_bcrs$sample_id <- sample_id

raw_bcrs %>%
  count(locus, productive, sort = TRUE) %>%
  head(10)
```

Now we'll filter the spAIRR data with `filterSpatialAirr()`, which is another function of
convenience to do the sort of filtering we've always done with spAIRR data. We have options to
filter for locus, min v, j, junction length, productivity, min consensus count, and we point
towards the spatial barcode column (technically optional argument).
We don't do it here, but we can also filter for max
opening gap in the seqeuence alignment column (max_opening_gap), and we can also add a
"full_id" (add_full_id) which combines the sequence_id and the spatial barcode columns.

Then I made another convenience function that plots the v, j, and junction lengths,
`plotLengthQc()`.  That's all it does, but we've often used those plots, so I figured why not.
spatialReceptorSummary is similar, it's a convenience function that prints the number of
sequences, spatial barcodes, loci, and productive sequences.

```{r filter-rad-output}
raw_igh <- filterSpatialAirr(
  raw_bcrs,
  loci = "IGH",
  min_v_length = 100,
  min_j_length = 10,
  min_junction_length = 1,
  productive_only = TRUE,
  min_consensus_count = 2,
  barcode_col = "barcode"
) %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(barcode),
    !is.na(sequence_alignment),
    sequence_alignment != ""
  )

plotLengthQc(raw_igh, bin_width = 5, title = "KH02 Length QC")
spatialReceptorSummary(raw_igh, barcode_col = "barcode")
```

# Presto Pipeline - processSpatialSample()

Before running `processSpatialSample()` and doing the major processing, we'll convert the
raw_igh dataframe into a fasta file using dowser's `dfToFasta()` function. We'll also pretend
that we want to carry a c_call column through the processing, so we add that to the sequence
id so that it gets written to the fasta header. We're not actually going to run this locally
because it takes a while.

`processSpatialSample()` takes the spAIRR processing pipeline we made and wraps it up in a
single R function.  It takes in a fasta file (and a lot of arguments for the different steps)
and returns a list of paths to the processed output.  This function is a wrapper around
* `ClusterSets.py set` groups reads within each spatial barcode `cluster_field`, the requested identity threshold `identity`, and vsearch. FASTA header delimiters are specified by `delimiters`.
* `ParseHeaders.py merge` is used to write a new field into the headers that combines the spatial barcode and the cluster id (provided with parse_fields). These are combined using `parse_act` (default cat) and written to a new header field `parse_key`.  Uses `delimiters` to specify the FASTA header delimiters.
* `AlignSets.py muscle` aligns reads within each `parse_key` group created by `ParseHeaders`. Takes `muscle_exec` as the path to the muscle aligner (https://github.com/rcedgar/muscle). Optionally logs results to `align_log`. Uses `delimiters` to specify the FASTA header delimiters.
* `BuildConsensus.py` creates consensus sequences within each `parse_key` group. `consensus_min_count` specifies the minimum number of sequences needed to define a valid consensus sequence, and `consensus_freq` specifies the fraction of character occurrences under which an ambiguous character is assigned. Optionally logs results to `consensus_log`. If there are additional fields in the FASTA header that should be carried forward and copied to the consensus file, `consensus_copy_fields` specifies the field names and `consensus_copy_action` specifies how to copy them (majority, first, last, or all).
* `AssignGenes.py igblast` assigns V(D)J gene annotations using IgBLAST. Takes either `ig` or `tr` as the argument to `receptor` (for bcr/tcr respectively). Takes `organism` as the argument to specify the species (e.g., human, mouse, etc.). `igblast_base` specifies the path to the IgBLAST installation, and `igblast_exec` can be provided if the igblast executable is not located in [`igblast_base`]/bin/igblastn.
* `MakeDb.py igblast` converts IgBLAST output to an AIRR-style TSV using the specified IMGT germline reference `germline_glob`.


```{r process-spatial-sample, eval=FALSE}
presto_input_dir <- file.path(walkthrough_dir, "processing_input")
presto_output_dir <- file.path(walkthrough_dir, "processing_output")
dir.create(presto_input_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
dir.create(presto_output_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

raw_igh <- fread(file.path(presto_input_dir, "filtered_igh.tsv"), data.table = FALSE)

raw_igh$c_call_for_header <- ifelse(
  is.na(raw_igh$c_call) | raw_igh$c_call == "",
  "NA",
  raw_igh$c_call
)
raw_igh$seq_id_c_call <- paste0(
  raw_igh$sequence_id,
  "|c_call_og:",
  raw_igh$c_call_for_header
)

presto_input_fasta <- file.path(presto_input_dir, "filtered_igh.fasta")
dowser::dfToFasta(
  raw_igh,
  file = presto_input_fasta,
  id = "seq_id_c_call",
  seq = "sequence_alignment"
)

processed_paths <- processSpatialSample(
  input_fasta = presto_input_fasta,
  output_dir = presto_output_dir,
  receptor = "ig",
  identity = 1.0,
  consensus_freq = 0.8,
  germline_glob = file.path(
    hunter_dir,
    "germlines/imgt/human/vdj/imgt_human_IG*.fasta"
  ),
  igblast_base = "~/software/igblast",
  muscle_exec = "~/software/muscle3.8.31_i86linux64",
  nproc = nproc,
  cluster_field = "barcode",
  delimiters = "'|' ':' ','",
  parse_fields = c("BARCODE", "CLUSTER"),
  parse_key = "BARCODECLUSTER",
  parse_act = "cat",
  consensus_min_count = 2,
  consensus_copy_fields = "C_CALL_OG",
  consensus_copy_action = "majority"
)
```

Now that we have the processed BCRs, we'll do a little more filtering with
`filterSpatialAirr()`, which ....  How much we really needed this function I'm not sure, but I did this
sort of filtering enough that I was okay with having it in the package.

```{r read-processed-bcrs}
processed_bcr_path <- file.path(
  thymus_dir,
  "sirap_visium_processing",
  sample_id,
  "bcr",
  "presto_output",
  paste0(
    "filtered_igh_ident_1.0_barcode_cluster_freq_0.8_cluster-pass_",
    "reheader_align-pass_consensus-pass_igblast_db-pass.tsv"
  )
)

processed_bcrs <- airr::read_rearrangement(processed_bcr_path)

processed_bcrs <- processed_bcrs %>%
  mutate(
    barcode = str_extract(sequence_id, "^[ACGT]{16}"),
    barcode_10x = paste0(barcode, "-1"),
    consensus_count = as.integer(str_match(sequence_id, "CONSCOUNT:([0-9]+)")[, 2]),
    receptor_type = "BCR"
  )

processed_bcrs <- filterSpatialAirr(
  processed_bcrs,
  loci = "IGH",
  min_v_length = 100,
  min_j_length = 10,
  min_junction_length = 1,
  productive_only = TRUE,
  min_consensus_count = 2,
  barcode_col = "barcode_10x"
)

spatialReceptorSummary(processed_bcrs, barcode_col = "barcode_10x")
summary(processed_bcrs$consensus_count)
```

# Load the spatial object

```{r load-seurat}
seurat_path <- file.path(
  thymus_dir,
  "data/240814_Visium/Intermediates/51T002-M5b/thy2_b_t_processed_seurat.rds"
)

mg_thymus_slice2 <- readRDS(seurat_path)
mg_thymus_slice2
```

# Check for identical sequences in neighboring spots

SIRAP can collapse the same sequence observed in neighboring spots. That is
useful for data types where adjacent barcodes are technical subdivisions of the
same biological unit. I show the diagnostic here, but I do not use its output
for Visium because neighboring spots are separate mixtures of cells.

`collapseTopConsensusPerBarcode()` is useful when we really want one
sequence per barcode and locus. I am not using it here. A Visium spot can
contain several cells and several real BCR sequences, so keeping only the most
abundant sequence would throw away real biology.

```{r neighboring-sequence-diagnostic}
image_name <- Images(mg_thymus_slice2)[1]
tissue_positions <- GetTissueCoordinates(
  mg_thymus_slice2[[image_name]],
  scale = image_scale
)
tissue_positions$barcode_10x <- rownames(tissue_positions)

if (!all(c("x", "y") %in% colnames(tissue_positions))) {
  stop("The tissue-coordinate table does not contain x and y columns.")
}

processed_bcrs_with_coordinates <- processed_bcrs %>%
  left_join(
    tissue_positions %>% select(barcode_10x, x, y),
    by = "barcode_10x"
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(x), !is.na(y))

neighbor_collapsed_bcrs <- collapseIdenticalNeighbors(
  data = processed_bcrs_with_coordinates,
  tissue_positions = tissue_positions,
  barcode = "barcode_10x",
  sequence = "sequence",
  consensus_count = "consensus_count",
  x = "x",
  y = "y"
)

tibble(
  version = c("original Visium table", "neighbor-collapsed diagnostic"),
  n_sequences = c(nrow(processed_bcrs_with_coordinates), nrow(neighbor_collapsed_bcrs)),
  n_spots = c(
    n_distinct(processed_bcrs_with_coordinates$barcode_10x),
    n_distinct(neighbor_collapsed_bcrs$barcode_10x)
  )
)

# Everything below continues with processed_bcrs, not neighbor_collapsed_bcrs.
```

# Make a SIRAP object

Clone IDs are optional in a SIRAP object, so I can make the object before clone
calling and add the clone field later.

```{r make-preclone-sirap-object}
mg_thymus_slice2_sirap <- createSIRAP(
  spatial = mg_thymus_slice2,
  receptors = processed_bcrs,
  barcode_col = "barcode_10x",
  clone_col = NULL,
  locus_col = "locus",
  count_col = "consensus_count",
  metadata = list(dataset = dataset, sample_id = sample_id)
)

mg_thymus_slice2_sirap
summary(mg_thymus_slice2_sirap)
spatialReceptorSummary(mg_thymus_slice2_sirap)

spatialObject(mg_thymus_slice2_sirap)
receptorTable(mg_thymus_slice2_sirap) %>% select(1:8) %>% head()
listAnalyses(mg_thymus_slice2_sirap)
```

# Build BCR clones

SIRAP does not replace `scoper`. The `withReceptors()` function passes the
receptor table to any function and returns that function's result. Its partner
`updateReceptors()` puts a data-frame result back into the SIRAP object. For
example, if I wanted to call clones using only the receptors already stored in
this object, I could do this:

```{r sample-only-clone-example, eval=FALSE}
sample_only_clones <- withReceptors(
  mg_thymus_slice2_sirap,
  scoper::hierarchicalClones,
  threshold = 0.1,
  cell_id = "sequence_id",
  summarize_clones = FALSE,
  nproc = nproc
)

mg_thymus_slice2_sirap <- updateReceptors(
  mg_thymus_slice2_sirap,
  scoper::hierarchicalClones,
  threshold = 0.1,
  cell_id = "sequence_id",
  summarize_clones = FALSE,
  nproc = nproc
)
```

The `with*()` version is useful when I want the result separately. The
`update*()` version returns a new SIRAP object with its receptor table replaced;
it does not modify the original object in place. When `hierarchicalClones()`
adds the usual `clone_id` column to an object made before clone calling,
`updateReceptors()` records that column as the SIRAP clone field automatically.

For this study, however, IGH clones were called jointly across both spatial
slices, matched bulk thymus, and matched blood. That keeps one clone ID universe
across all of those samples, so I make the combined table first and call
`scoper` on that table.

```{r build-clones, eval=FALSE}
all_igh <- bind_rows(
  spatial_igh_kh01,
  spatial_igh_kh02,
  bulk_thymus_igh,
  blood_igh
) %>%
  filter(
    productive,
    locus == "IGH",
    !is.na(v_call),
    v_call != "",
    !is.na(j_call),
    j_call != "",
    !is.na(junction),
    junction != ""
  ) %>%
  mutate(tissue_seq_id = paste0(tissue_sample, "_", sequence_id))

all_igh_clones <- scoper::hierarchicalClones(
  all_igh,
  threshold = 0.1,
  cell_id = "tissue_seq_id",
  summarize_clones = FALSE,
  nproc = nproc
)

saveRDS(
  all_igh_clones,
  file.path(walkthrough_dir, "clones_thymus_spatial_bulk_igh.rds")
)
```

The joint clone call has already been run, so I load it and take the KH02 rows
for the spatial walkthrough.

```{r load-clones}
clone_path <- file.path(
  thymus_dir,
  "sirap_visium_processing/clones/clones_thymus_spatial_bulk_igh.rds"
)

all_igh_clones <- readRDS(clone_path)

mg_thymus_slice2_bcr_clones <- all_igh_clones %>%
  filter(tissue_sample == "visium_thymus_KH02") %>%
  mutate(
    barcode = str_extract(sequence_id, "^[ACGT]{16}"),
    barcode_10x = paste0(barcode, "-1"),
    consensus_count = coalesce(
      as.numeric(consensus_count),
      as.numeric(str_match(sequence_id, "CONSCOUNT:([0-9]+)")[, 2])
    )
  )

mg_thymus_slice2_bcr_clones <- mg_thymus_slice2_bcr_clones %>%
  mutate(
    clone_id = as.character(clone_id),
    receptor_type = "BCR"
  )

clone_counts <- mg_thymus_slice2_bcr_clones %>%
  filter(!is.na(clone_id)) %>%
  group_by(clone_id) %>%
  summarize(
    n_sequences = n(),
    n_spots = n_distinct(barcode_10x),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(n_spots), desc(n_sequences))

clone_counts %>% head(10)
```

I add the jointly inferred clone assignment to the receptor table already in
the SIRAP object. The explicit mapping is optional here because the conventional
name is `clone_id`, but I show it so that the same pattern is clear for studies
that use another clone-column name.

```{r update-sirap-with-clones}
clone_assignments <- mg_thymus_slice2_bcr_clones %>%
  select(sequence_id, clone_id) %>%
  distinct()

mg_thymus_slice2_sirap <- updateReceptors(
  mg_thymus_slice2_sirap,
  dplyr::left_join,
  y = clone_assignments,
  by = "sequence_id",
  receptor_fields = list(clone = "clone_id")
)

mg_thymus_slice2_sirap
```

# Plot expression and BCRs

```{r basic-spatial-plots}
demo_clone_id <- clone_counts %>%
  filter(n_spots >= 3) %>%
  slice_head(n = 1) %>%
  pull(clone_id)

gex_plot <- spatialExpressionPlot(
  mg_thymus_slice2_sirap,
  features = "AICDA",
  assay = "alra",
  layer = "data",
  image.scale = image_scale,
  swap_coords = swap_coords
)

all_bcr_plot <- plotReceptors(
  mg_thymus_slice2_sirap,
  group_col = "receptor_type",
  values = "BCR",
  colors = "#0072B2",
  receptor_size = 1.5,
  image.scale = image_scale,
  swap_coords = swap_coords,
  title = "All BCR-positive spots"
)

gex_bcr_plot <- plotReceptorsExpression(
  mg_thymus_slice2_sirap,
  group_col = "receptor_type",
  values = "BCR",
  feature = "AICDA",
  assay = "alra",
  layer = "data",
  colors = "#0072B2",
  image.scale = image_scale,
  swap_coords = swap_coords,
  title = "AICDA expression and BCR-positive spots"
)

clone_plot <- plotReceptors(
  mg_thymus_slice2_sirap,
  group_col = "clone_id",
  values = demo_clone_id,
  colors = "#D55E00",
  receptor_size = 1.8,
  image.scale = image_scale,
  swap_coords = swap_coords,
  title = paste("BCR clone", demo_clone_id)
)

cowplot::plot_grid(gex_plot, all_bcr_plot, gex_bcr_plot, clone_plot, ncol = 2)
```

# Add the cell-type deconvolution results

The CARD proportions remain continuous. I attach all of them to the Seurat
metadata instead of assigning every mixed spot one dominant cell type.

```{r attach-card-results}
card_path <- file.path(
  thymus_dir,
  "data/240814_Visium/51T002-M5b/Cell_Type_Decon_CARD/CARD_thy2_b.rds"
)

card_thymus_slice2 <- readRDS(card_path)
card_proportions <- as.data.frame(card_thymus_slice2@Proportion_CARD)
card_proportions <- card_proportions[
  colnames(spatialObject(mg_thymus_slice2_sirap)),
  ,
  drop = FALSE
]

# withSpatial() would return the updated Seurat object by itself. Here I want
# to keep it in the SIRAP object, so I use updateSpatial().
mg_thymus_slice2_sirap <- updateSpatial(
  mg_thymus_slice2_sirap,
  SeuratObject::AddMetaData,
  metadata = card_proportions
)

spatialObject(mg_thymus_slice2_sirap)@meta.data %>%
  select(`GC B`, T, `Proliferating GC B`, `Naive B`) %>%
  summary()
```

# Moran's I and local Moran's I

I use the same neighborhood definition for global and local Moran's I. The
gene example uses AICDA expression and the cell-type example uses the
continuous CARD GC B-cell proportion.

```{r morans-i}
aicda_moran <- spatialMoran(
  mg_thymus_slice2_sirap,
  variable = "AICDA",
  variable_type = "feature",
  layer = "data",
  k = 6
)
aicda_moran$test

gc_b_moran <- spatialMoran(
  mg_thymus_slice2_sirap,
  variable = "GC B",
  variable_type = "metadata",
  k = 6
)
gc_b_moran$test

mg_thymus_slice2_sirap <- setAnalysis(
  mg_thymus_slice2_sirap,
  "morans_i",
  list(AICDA = aicda_moran, GC_B = gc_b_moran)
)
```

```{r local-morans-i}
aicda_local_moran <- spatialLocalMoran(
  mg_thymus_slice2_sirap,
  variable = "AICDA",
  variable_type = "feature",
  layer = "data",
  k = 6
)

gc_b_local_moran <- spatialLocalMoran(
  mg_thymus_slice2_sirap,
  variable = "GC B",
  variable_type = "metadata",
  k = 6
)

mg_thymus_slice2_sirap <- setAnalysis(
  mg_thymus_slice2_sirap,
  "local_morans_i",
  list(AICDA = aicda_local_moran, GC_B = gc_b_local_moran)
)

aicda_local_plot <- plotSpatialLocalMoran(
  mg_thymus_slice2_sirap,
  aicda_local_moran,
  image.scale = image_scale,
  swap_coords = swap_coords,
  title = "AICDA local Moran's I"
)

gc_b_local_plot <- plotSpatialLocalMoran(
  mg_thymus_slice2_sirap,
  gc_b_local_moran,
  image.scale = image_scale,
  swap_coords = swap_coords,
  title = "GC B-cell proportion local Moran's I"
)

cowplot::plot_grid(aicda_local_plot, gc_b_local_plot, ncol = 2)
```

# Ripley's cross K

For this analysis I say that a spot contains a cell type when its CARD
proportion is greater than 10%. A spot above 10% for both cell types is left
out of this pairwise marked-point analysis because `Kcross` assigns one mark to
each point.

```{r ripley-marks}
mg_thymus_slice2_sirap <- updateSpatial(
  mg_thymus_slice2_sirap,
  function(spatial) {
    spatial$gc_b_present <- spatial$`GC B` > 0.10
    spatial$t_cell_present <- spatial$T > 0.10
    spatial$ripley_gc_b_t_mark <- dplyr::case_when(
      spatial$gc_b_present & !spatial$t_cell_present ~ "GC B > 10%",
      spatial$t_cell_present & !spatial$gc_b_present ~ "T > 10%",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
    spatial
  }
)

table(
  spatialObject(mg_thymus_slice2_sirap)$ripley_gc_b_t_mark,
  useNA = "ifany"
)
```

```{r ripley-cross-k}
gc_b_t_k <- spatialRipleyCrossK(
  mg_thymus_slice2_sirap,
  mark_col = "ripley_gc_b_t_mark",
  i = "GC B > 10%",
  j = "T > 10%",
  nsim = 99,
  max_r = 500
)

mg_thymus_slice2_sirap <- setAnalysis(
  mg_thymus_slice2_sirap,
  "ripley_gc_b_t",
  gc_b_t_k
)

plotRipleyCrossK(
  gc_b_t_k,
  title = "Ripley's cross K: GC B-cell and T-cell containing spots"
)
```

# Join count for one B-cell clone

The join-count test asks whether receptor-positive neighboring spots are more
likely to contain the same clone than expected under random labeling. I return
the barcode-level data because the plotting function uses the exact spots and
neighbor graph from the test.

```{r clone-join-count}
join_count_clone_id <- clone_counts %>%
  filter(n_spots >= 3) %>%
  slice_head(n = 1) %>%
  pull(clone_id)

clone_join_count <- spatialCloneJoinCount(
  object = mg_thymus_slice2_sirap,
  clone_ids = join_count_clone_id,
  min_barcodes = 3,
  k = 6,
  alternative = "greater",
  return_data = TRUE
)

clone_join_count$summary

mg_thymus_slice2_sirap <- setAnalysis(
  mg_thymus_slice2_sirap,
  "clone_join_count",
  clone_join_count
)

# withAnalysis() can inspect or summarize a stored result without removing it.
withAnalysis(
  mg_thymus_slice2_sirap,
  "clone_join_count",
  function(result) result$summary
)

plotSpatialCloneJoinCount(
  join_count = clone_join_count,
  object = mg_thymus_slice2_sirap,
  clone_id = join_count_clone_id,
  image.scale = image_scale,
  swap_coords = swap_coords,
  show_neighbors = TRUE
)
```

# Select or load GC polygons

I already saved these GC polygons, so the walkthrough reads them directly. If
the CSV is not present, the same code falls back to the interactive SIRAP
polygon selector.

```{r load-or-select-polygons}
polygon_path <- file.path(
  thymus_dir,
  "plots/gc_clonal_dominance/mg_thymus_slice2",
  "mg_thymus_slice2_gc_polygons_vertices.csv"
)

if (file.exists(polygon_path)) {
  mg_thymus_slice2_polygons <- fread(polygon_path) %>% as.data.frame()
} else {
  mg_thymus_slice2_polygons <- selectSpatialPolygons(
    object = mg_thymus_slice2_sirap,
    assay = "alra",
    layer = "data",
    feature = "AICDA",
    image.scale = image_scale,
    swap_coords = swap_coords,
    save_path = polygon_path,
    host = "0.0.0.0",
    port = 8788L,
    plot_image = TRUE,
    launch.browser = FALSE
  )
}

plotSpatialPolygons(
  object = mg_thymus_slice2_sirap,
  polygon = mg_thymus_slice2_polygons,
  image.scale = image_scale,
  swap_coords = swap_coords,
  polygon_alpha = 0.2
)
```

# Clonal dominance inside the GC polygons

```{r clonal-dominance}
gc_clonal_dominance <- spatialCloneDominance(
  object = mg_thymus_slice2_sirap,
  polygon = mg_thymus_slice2_polygons,
  locus = "IGH",
  image.scale = image_scale,
  swap_coords = swap_coords,
  exclude_singletons = FALSE
)

gc_clonal_dominance_no_singletons <- spatialCloneDominance(
  object = mg_thymus_slice2_sirap,
  polygon = mg_thymus_slice2_polygons,
  locus = "IGH",
  image.scale = image_scale,
  swap_coords = swap_coords,
  exclude_singletons = TRUE
)

mg_thymus_slice2_sirap <- setAnalysis(
  mg_thymus_slice2_sirap,
  "gc_clonal_dominance",
  gc_clonal_dominance
)

# updateAnalysis() applies a function to one stored result and saves the result
# back under the same name. Here I add the sample identifier to its metadata.
mg_thymus_slice2_sirap <- updateAnalysis(
  mg_thymus_slice2_sirap,
  "gc_clonal_dominance",
  function(result, sample_id) {
    result$metadata$sample_id <- sample_id
    result
  },
  sample_id = sample_id
)

withAnalysis(
  mg_thymus_slice2_sirap,
  "gc_clonal_dominance",
  function(result) result$dominance
) %>%
  arrange(polygon, desc(proportion)) %>%
  group_by(polygon) %>%
  slice_head(n = 5)
```

# Build and plot BCR trees

I pick a few expanded clones that are large enough to make an interesting tree
but small enough to read on a slide.

```{r choose-tree-clones}
tree_clone_ids <- mg_thymus_slice2_bcr_clones %>%
  filter(!is.na(clone_id), !is.na(sequence_alignment), sequence_alignment != "") %>%
  group_by(clone_id) %>%
  summarize(
    n_sequences = n(),
    n_unique_sequences = n_distinct(sequence_alignment),
    n_spots = n_distinct(barcode_10x),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  filter(
    n_sequences >= 8,
    n_sequences <= 15,
    n_unique_sequences >= 5,
    n_spots >= 2
  ) %>%
  arrange(n_sequences, desc(n_unique_sequences), desc(n_spots)) %>%
  slice_head(n = 3) %>%
  pull(clone_id)

clone_counts %>% filter(clone_id %in% tree_clone_ids)
```

```{r build-trees}
tree_path <- file.path(walkthrough_dir, "mg_thymus_slice2_bcr_trees.rds")

if (!file.exists(tree_path)) {
  imgt_refs <- dowser::readIMGT(
    file.path(hunter_dir, "germlines/imgt/human/vdj")
  )

  tree_input <- mg_thymus_slice2_bcr_clones %>%
    filter(clone_id %in% tree_clone_ids)

  tree_input <- dowser::createGermlines(
    tree_input,
    imgt_refs,
    id = "sequence_id"
  )

  formatted_clones <- dowser::formatClones(
    tree_input,
    id = "sequence_id",
    germ = "germline_alignment",
    traits = "barcode_10x",
    filterstop = FALSE,
    collapse = TRUE,
    add_count = TRUE,
    num_fields = "consensus_count"
  )

  bcr_trees <- dowser::getTrees(
    formatted_clones,
    nproc = 1
  )

  saveRDS(bcr_trees, tree_path)
} else {
  bcr_trees <- readRDS(tree_path)
}

mg_thymus_slice2_sirap <- setAnalysis(
  mg_thymus_slice2_sirap,
  "dowser_trees",
  bcr_trees
)

listAnalyses(mg_thymus_slice2_sirap)
```

First I give each tree tip its own color and use the same colors at its spatial
location.

```{r plot-tree-spatial-pairs}
tree_spatial_pairs <- plotSpatialCloneTreePairs(
  bcr_trees,
  object = mg_thymus_slice2_sirap,
  clone_ids = tree_clone_ids,
  id_col = "sequence_id",
  image.scale = image_scale,
  swap_coords = swap_coords,
  treescale = 0.01,
  zoom = FALSE
)

first_tree_clone <- names(tree_spatial_pairs)[1]
cowplot::plot_grid(
  tree_spatial_pairs[[first_tree_clone]]$tree,
  tree_spatial_pairs[[first_tree_clone]]$spatial_clone,
  ncol = 2,
  rel_widths = c(1.2, 1)
)
```

For a larger tree, I can use SIRAP to group genetically related tips and carry
those group colors onto the tissue.

```{r cluster-and-plot-tree-tips}
clustered_bcr_trees <- clusterTreesTips(
  bcr_trees,
  k = "auto",
  id_col = "sequence_id",
  cluster_col = "tree_cluster",
  k_range = 2:8,
  cut_terminal_edges = FALSE
)

clustered_tree_spatial_pairs <- plotSpatialCloneTreePairs(
  clustered_bcr_trees,
  object = mg_thymus_slice2_sirap,
  clone_ids = tree_clone_ids,
  id_col = "sequence_id",
  color_by = "tree_cluster",
  image.scale = image_scale,
  swap_coords = swap_coords,
  treescale = 0.01,
  zoom = FALSE
)

first_tree_clone <- names(clustered_tree_spatial_pairs)[1]
cowplot::plot_grid(
  clustered_tree_spatial_pairs[[first_tree_clone]]$tree,
  clustered_tree_spatial_pairs[[first_tree_clone]]$spatial_clone,
  ncol = 2,
  rel_widths = c(1.2, 1)
)
```

```{r save-all-tree-pairs, eval=FALSE}
spatialCloneTreePairsToPDF(
  trees = clustered_bcr_trees,
  object = mg_thymus_slice2_sirap,
  file = file.path(walkthrough_dir, "mg_thymus_slice2_tree_spatial_pairs.pdf"),
  clone_ids = tree_clone_ids,
  id_col = "sequence_id",
  color_by = "tree_cluster",
  image.scale = image_scale,
  swap_coords = swap_coords,
  treescale = 0.01
)
```
